law: combustion and the calcination of metals consist in the escape of phlogiston, as Stahl taught and all chemists hold
obs: tin and lead calcined in sealed vessels gain weight by the balance, by exactly as much as the enclosed air loses

law: heat is a subtle fluid, caloric, which can be neither created nor destroyed, as Lavoisier and Laplace maintain
obs: in the boring of cannon heat is drawn out by friction without limit for as long as the work continues, and the metal chips show no change in their capacity for heat

law: animalcules and the lower forms of life arise of themselves from decaying matter, as Aristotle taught and Needham confirmed
obs: broth boiled in a flask whose neck is drawn out into a bent tube open to the air stays barren for years, yet teems within days once the neck is broken off

law: the cholera is caused by a miasma rising from filth, as the Board of Health and the best physicians hold
obs: in one London parish the deaths lie almost wholly among those who drew water from a single street pump, while brewers' men and workhouse inmates breathing the same air, having their own wells, escape, and the deaths cease when the pump handle is removed

law: the sun and all the planets circle the earth, which rests at the centre, as Ptolemy and Aristotle teach
obs: the planet Venus, seen through the telescope, passes through a full round of phases like the moon, appearing small and round when full and large and horned when new

law: heavy bodies fall faster than light ones in proportion to their weight, as Aristotle laid down
obs: balls of very unequal weight let fall together from a tower reach the ground so nearly at the same instant that the difference is a hand's breadth

law: nature abhors a vacuum, and by this abhorrence water rises in a pump, as the schools have taught since Aristotle
obs: no pump will raise water higher than about thirty-four feet, and quicksilver in a closed tube stands at thirty inches and leaves an empty space above it, standing lower upon a mountain top

law: light consists of corpuscles shot out from luminous bodies, as Newton maintained
obs: light passed through two near slits makes alternate bright and dark bands where the beams overlap, so that light added to light gives darkness, and light is found to travel slower in water than in air

law: the substances of living bodies can be formed only by a vital force within the organism, as Berzelius teaches
obs: urea, identical in every property with that of the animal body, is obtained in the laboratory by heating a salt prepared from mineral matter alone

law: every species was separately created and remains fixed within narrow limits, as Linnaeus and Cuvier hold
obs: the rocks show a long succession of forms graded one into another, islands bear species peculiar to each yet near akin to those of the nearest mainland, and breeders by selection produce races differing more than many wild species

law: inflammatory fevers are cured by copious bleeding, the practice of Galen upheld by Broussais and the whole faculty
obs: when the cases of pneumonia in a hospital are counted, those bled early and freely die as often as those bled late or not at all

law: the planets move in perfect circles, or circles compounded upon circles, as all astronomers from Plato to Copernicus have held
obs: the places of Mars observed by Tycho over twenty years depart by eight minutes of arc from the best that any arrangement of circles can give, and Tycho's instruments are trusted to two minutes

law: the heavens beyond the moon are perfect and unchangeable, as Aristotle teaches
obs: a new star blazes out in Cassiopeia, brighter than Venus, and fades over sixteen months, showing no parallax whatever from any station in Europe

law: the blood is made continually in the liver from food and consumed in the members, as Galen teaches
obs: the heart at each beat throws out some two ounces of blood, so that in half an hour it passes more than the whole body contains and far more than any food could supply, and a bound vein swells on the side away from the heart

law: water is a simple element, one of the four, as held from Empedocles and Aristotle onward
obs: when inflammable air is burnt with vital air in a closed globe, pure water is deposited equal in weight to the two airs consumed, and steam passed over red-hot iron yields the inflammable air again

law: the earth is some six thousand years old, as the chronology of Archbishop Ussher establishes
obs: strata many thousands of feet thick, laid down layer upon layer as slowly as rivers lay their mud to-day, are found tilted, worn down, and buried again beneath later strata

law: basalt and all the rocks were precipitated from a universal ocean, as Werner teaches at Freiberg
obs: in Auvergne sheets of basalt are traced step by step up the valleys to craters of cinders, and are found to have baked the clays beneath them

law: childbed fever arises from an epidemic influence of the atmosphere, as the professors of midwifery teach
obs: of two lying-in wards under one roof, that served by students coming from the dissecting-room loses five times as many women as that served by midwives, and the deaths fall at once when the students wash their hands in chlorinated lime

law: the scurvy arises from the damp and foul air of ships, as the College of Physicians holds
obs: of twelve scorbutic seamen kept in one berth upon one diet, the two given oranges and lemons are fit for duty in six days while the rest grow worse

law: electricity and magnetism are wholly distinct powers having no action upon one another, as Coulomb demonstrated
obs: a compass needle placed near a wire is turned aside whenever a galvanic current passes through the wire, and returns when the current ceases

law: light passes instantaneously across any distance, as Descartes maintains
obs: the eclipses of Jupiter's first satellite fall behind the tables by some minutes as the earth recedes from Jupiter and gain again as it approaches, year after year

law: stones cannot fall from the sky, there being none there to fall, as the Academy of Sciences has resolved
obs: at L'Aigle in Normandy, in full daylight, some thousands of stones fall over a space of leagues after a fireball and loud explosions, before the whole countryside, and the stones are alike among themselves and unlike any rock of the district

law: the great boulders and gravels scattered over northern Europe were borne by the waters of the Deluge, as Buckland and the diluvial school teach
obs: the boulders rest on rock polished and scored in straight parallel grooves, exactly as beneath the glaciers of the Alps, and lie in ridges like the moraines at a glacier's foot

law: potash and soda are simple elements incapable of decomposition, being so listed by Lavoisier
obs: when the current of a powerful voltaic battery is passed through moistened potash, bright metallic globules appear at the negative wire, which burn upon water and form potash again

law: oxygen is the principle of acidity and is present in every acid, as Lavoisier established in naming it
obs: muriatic acid, tried by charcoal at a white heat and by every means that takes oxygen from other bodies, yields none, and is formed from hydrogen and chlorine alone

law: the ague is caused by bad air rising from marshes, whence its name malaria, as physicians have held since Hippocrates
obs: the parasite of the ague is found developing in the stomach wall of a particular mosquito fed upon a patient, and men sleeping in the marshes behind fine wire gauze remain well while their neighbours sicken

law: the speed of sound in air is given by Newton's calculation in the Principia from the elasticity and density of the air
obs: the speed measured with cannon over known distances, by many observers in several countries, exceeds the calculated speed by one sixth

law: the distances of the planets from the sun follow the progression of Titius and Bode, confirmed by the discovery of Uranus and of Ceres
obs: the planet Neptune is found at thirty times the earth's distance, where the progression requires nearly thirty-nine

law: the atomic weights of all the elements are exact multiples of that of hydrogen, according to Prout's hypothesis
obs: the atomic weight of chlorine, determined by Stas with the utmost refinement and by several methods, comes out always 35.5

law: characters acquired by the parent through use or injury are transmitted to the offspring, as Lamarck taught
obs: mice whose tails are cut off at birth for nineteen generations bear young with tails of full length in every case

law: the muscles are moved by animal spirits flowing into them through the hollow nerves, as Galen and Descartes teach
obs: a muscle made to contract under water in a closed glass vessel does not raise the level of the water at all

law: a pendulum of given length beats in the same time in every place, as Galileo and Huygens proved
obs: a clock regulated at Paris loses two and a half minutes a day when carried to Cayenne, and its pendulum must be shortened there, the same being found on later voyages toward the equator

law: Newton's law of universal gravitation, by the inverse square of the distance, governs exactly the motions of all the planets
obs: the planet Uranus departs from its computed place by more than a minute of arc, after every allowance for Jupiter and Saturn, and the error grows from year to year

law: the comet of 1682 returns in a fixed period under the sun's attraction, as Halley computed from Newton's principles
obs: the comet does not appear at the time computed for its return, and month after month passes without it

law: the earth revolves yearly about the sun, as Copernicus teaches
obs: the fixed stars show no yearly shifting of their places, though the earth is said to cross an orbit of vast breadth

law: the attraction of gravity varies exactly as the inverse square of the distance, as Newton laid down
obs: the motion of the moon's apogee, computed from this law by Clairaut, Euler and d'Alembert each separately, comes out only half of what is observed

law: a star moves uniformly in a straight line unless some body attracts it, by Newton's laws of motion
obs: Sirius is found to move in a wavy line across the sky, swinging to and fro in a period of fifty years, with no companion visible in any telescope

law: the living force of moving bodies is never lost, as Leibniz and the Bernoullis maintain
obs: when two balls of soft lead collide and stop dead, their living force vanishes altogether and nothing visible receives it

law: matter is neither created nor destroyed in any chemical change, the principle of Lavoisier
obs: a log burnt upon the open hearth leaves ashes weighing but a small fraction of the wood

law: living things arise only from parents of their own kind, as Redi showed
obs: mutton gravy boiled, corked and sealed with mastic is found after some days swarming with animalcules

law: the hand of one person exerts no force upon the nerves of another at a distance, there being no magnetic fluid of the kind known to natural philosophy
obs: patients touched by the magnetiser, or led to trees he has magnetised, fall into convulsions and declare themselves cured

law: a body at rest is not set in motion except by a force applied to it, by the first law of motion
obs: tables about which a company sit with hands laid lightly upon them turn and travel across the room, the sitters all declaring that they do not push

law: a pure gas has one fixed density whatever its source, as all chemistry assumes
obs: nitrogen drawn from the air is constantly heavier, by one part in two hundred, than nitrogen prepared from ammonia, in the hands of Lord Rayleigh over two years

law: the properties of the elements are a periodic function of their atomic weights, as Mendeleeff's law declares
obs: the accepted atomic weight of indium, 75.6, would place it between arsenic and selenium, where there is no vacant place and where its properties do not belong

law: equal volumes of all gases contain equal numbers of molecules, the law of Avogadro
obs: the vapour of sal-ammoniac has but half the density which its formula requires

law: water is not changed into earth by any amount of boiling, the two being distinct substances, as Boerhaave held
obs: water distilled over and over for a hundred days in a glass vessel leaves each time an earthy sediment

law: no machine can give out more work than is put into it, as the Academy of Sciences declared in refusing all schemes of perpetual motion
obs: a machine exhibited in Philadelphia runs day after day with no visible supply of power, before paying crowds

law: the planets keep their mean motions unchanged for ever under Newton's law of gravitation
obs: Jupiter has been gaining speed and Saturn losing it for centuries, as Halley found, so that the tables of both go steadily wrong

law: the osmotic pressure of a dissolved substance equals that of a gas having the same number of molecules, the law of van 't Hoff
obs: solutions of common salt and of other salts press nearly twice as hard as the law allows

law: light is a wave, as Fresnel's memoir maintains
obs: it follows from the theory, as Poisson has calculated, that the centre of the shadow of a small round disc should be as bright as if no disc were there, which he declares absurd

law: the blood passes from the arteries into the veins and so returns to the heart, as Harvey teaches
obs: no passage from the arteries into the veins can be found by the most careful dissection

law: the earth turns daily upon its axis, as Copernicus teaches
obs: a stone dropped from the top of a tower falls at its foot, and is not left behind to the west

law: the cholera is caused by the comma bacillus, as Koch has shown
obs: a professor of hygiene swallows a full culture of the bacillus and suffers no more than a slight looseness

law: energy cannot be created, the principle of Mayer and Joule
obs: the sun pours out heat without stint age after age, though a globe of the best coal of its size would be burnt out in five thousand years

law: species descend from earlier species by slow modification, as Darwin maintains
obs: between the well-marked species of successive formations the connecting forms are for the most part wanting

law: the cow-pox protects against the small-pox, as Jenner showed
obs: some persons vaccinated in infancy take the small-pox in later life
